title: Project 2 - Static EDA
text:
Data Setup
Import downloaded raw CSV data.
Convert to R-friendly variable names using the janitor package, and force data to classic tibble structure (instead of spc_tbl_ )

mxmh_raw <- read_csv("data/mxmh_survey_results.csv")

Basic data cleaning:

assign categorical data as factors (some ordinal)
derive musician status as a composite of instrumentalist and composer
drop permissions variable (all records granted permission)
drop timestamp variable (not relevant for analysis)


mxmh <- mxmh_raw |>
  mutate(
    #Nominal factors:
    primary_streaming_service = as.factor(primary_streaming_service),
    fav_genre =as.factor(fav_genre),
    
    #Yes/No categorical:
    across(c("while_working", "instrumentalist", "composer", "exploratory", "foreign_languages"),
           function(x) factor(x, levels=c("Yes", "No"))),
    
    #Freq categorical:
    across(starts_with("frequency_"),
           function(x) factor(x, levels=c("Never", "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Very frequently"), ordered=TRUE)),
    
    #Effect categorical:
    music_effects = factor(music_effects, levels=c("Improve", "No effect", "Worsen"), ordered=TRUE),
    
    #Derive musician status:
    musician = case_when(
      instrumentalist == "Yes" & composer== "Yes" ~ "Instrumentalist and Composer",
      instrumentalist =="Yes"  ~ "Instrumentalist Only",
      composer == "Yes"  ~ "Composer Only",
      TRUE ~ "Other/Non-Musician")
    ) |> 
  select(-permissions, -timestamp)

Save cleaned data to repo for future access:

save(mxmh, file="data/mxmh.RData")

Load the helper.R file with variable lists and labels. (Note: This file is mainly used by the app, but it was operationally tested for the static Heatmap plot.)

title: Project 2 - Static EDA
text:
Numeric EDA

Contingency Tables
Use tidy summary methods with results stored in tibbles to simplify reporting on the app.
One-Way:

tab_one <- mxmh |> 
  drop_na(fav_genre) |>
  group_by(fav_genre) |>
  summarize(count=n(), .groups = "drop")

Summary Stats
Again, use tidy methods with tibble result storage to simplify the app. I chose to report mean, sd, min, median, max.

tab_sum <- mxmh |>
  drop_na(frequency_classical) |>
  group_by(frequency_classical) |>
  select(frequency_classical, anxiety, age) |>
  summarize(across(where(is.numeric),
            list("Mean"   = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "SD"     = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "Min"    = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "Median" = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "Max"    = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .names = "{.fn}_{.col}")
  )

title: Project 2 - Static EDA
text:
Visual EDA

Density Plots
For a numeric variable, with the option for 1 categorical variable as a facet.
Univariate:

ggplot(mxmh |> drop_na(age)) +
  geom_density(aes(x=age), fill="#009e73") + 
  labs(title="Density of Age",
       x="Age", y="Density") +
  scale_fill_discrete("Listening Frequency: Classical") +
  theme_minimal() 








Multivariate:

ggplot(mxmh |> drop_na(age, frequency_classical)) +
  geom_density(aes(x=age, fill=frequency_classical)) +
  facet_wrap(~ frequency_classical) +
  labs(title="Density of Age x Classical Listening Frequency",
       x="Age", y="Density") +
  scale_fill_discrete("Listening Frequency: Classical")+ 
  theme_minimal() 










Boxplots
For a numeric variable, with the option for 1 categorical variable as a within-plot grouping.
Univariate:

ggplot(mxmh |> drop_na(age),
       aes(y=age)) +
  geom_boxplot(width=0.2, fill="#009e73") + 
  scale_x_discrete() +  #for univariate only
  labs(title="Boxplot of Age",
       y="Age") +
  theme_minimal() 








Multivariate:

ggplot(mxmh |> drop_na(age, frequency_classical),
       aes(x=frequency_classical, y=age, fill=frequency_classical)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(title="Boxplot of Age x Classical Listening Frequency",
       x="Listening Frequency: Classical", y="Age") +
  scale_fill_discrete("Listening Frequency: Classical") + 
  theme_minimal()










Bar Charts
Frequency bar charts for 1-2 categorical variables.
If a second categorical variable is provided, that variable serves as a grouping effect for side-by-side bar chart layout.
One-way:

ggplot(mxmh, aes(x=frequency_classical)) +
  geom_bar(fill="#009e73") + 
  labs(title="Bar Chart of Classical Listening Frequency",
       x="Listening Frequency: Classical", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()








Two-way:

ggplot(mxmh, aes(x=frequency_classical)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill=composer), position="dodge") +
  labs(title="Bar Chart of Classical Listening Frequency by Composer Status",
       x="Listening Frequency: Classical", y = "Count") +
  scale_fill_discrete("Composer Status") +
  theme_minimal()










Heatmap
A visualization of frequency concentrations for a two-way contingency table. Not available for single-variable reporting.
Plotted on a monochromatic scale: lighter shading for lower frequency, darker shading for higher frequency.

tab_two <- as.data.frame(table(mxmh$music_effects, mxmh$while_working))

ggplot(as.data.frame(tab_two), aes(x = Var1, y=Var2, fill=Freq)) +
  geom_tile(color="black") +
  #force an extreme monochrome scale
  scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high="#006b4e")  +
  #example of using helpers to apply variable names:
  labs(x = names(vars_all[which(vars_all=="music_effects")]),
       y = names(vars_all[which(vars_all=="while_working")])) +
  theme_minimal()
